1          Having reviewed the parties’ submissions, the Court hereby ORDERS that Plaintiffs’
2    Unopposed Motion for Consolidation and appointment of Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel is
3    GRANTED.
4           IT IS HEREBY ORDERED THAT:
5           1.     Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42, the Dolphin v. Hims & Hers, Inc.,
6    No. 3:26-cv-03077-CRB (“Dolphin”) and Hoagland-Sweeney v. Hims & Hers Health, Inc. No.
7    3:26cv3157 (“Hoagland-Sweeney”) are consolidated for all purposes. The Dolphin case is
8    designated as the lead case. All papers filed in the Consolidated Action shall be filed under Case
9    No.: 3:26-cv-03077-CRB and shall bear the following caption:
10                                 UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
                                 NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA
11
12   IN RE HIMS & HERS, INC. DATA BREACH Lead Case No.: 3:26-cv-03077-CRB
     LITIGATION
13
14   This Document Relates To:

15
16          2.     All future pleadings, motions, briefs, and other papers shall be filed in Case No.

17   3:26-cv-03077-CRB. The Clerk is directed to CLOSE Case No. 3:26cv3157.

18          3.     All future filed or transferred actions that are related to the Consolidated Action

19   pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42 in that they are based on the same or similar facts

20   and circumstances shall be consolidated in the Consolidated Action upon agreement of the

21   parties and the filing of a notice of consolidation.

22          4.     Interim Co-Lead Counsel Daniel Srourian of Srourian Law Firm, P.C. and Scott

23   Edward Cole of Cole & Van Note shall be responsible for the overall conduct of the litigation on

24   behalf of the proposed class, including providing supervision of all Plaintiffs’ counsel in this

25   litigation. As Interim Co-Lead Counsel for Plaintiffs, Daniel Srourian and Scott Edward Cole

26   have the authority to:

27                 a. Coordinate the work of preparing and presenting all of Plaintiffs’ claims and
                      otherwise coordinating all proceedings, including organizing and supervising
28
                                     -2-
         [PROPOSED] ORDER GRANTING PLAINTIFFS’ UNOPPOSED MOTION FOR
       CONSOLIDATION AND APPOINTMENT OF INTERIM CO-LEAD CLASS COUNSEL
      Case 3:26-cv-03077-CRB        Document 26         Filed 08/10/26      Page 3 of 4




1                    the efforts of Plaintiffs’ counsel in a manner to ensure that Plaintiffs’ pretrial
                     preparation is conducted effectively, efficiently, expeditiously and
2                    economically;
3                 b. Delegate work responsibilities and monitoring the activities of all Plaintiffs’
                     counsel in a manner to promote the orderly and efficient conduct of this
4                    litigation and to avoid unnecessary duplication and expense;
5                 c. Call meetings of Plaintiffs’ counsel for any appropriate purpose, including
                     coordinating responses to questions of other parties or of the Court, and
6                    initiating proposals, suggestions, schedules and any other appropriate matters;
7                 d. Determine (after consultation with other co-counsel as may be appropriate) and
                     present (in briefs, oral argument or such other fashion as he or his designee may
8                    deem appropriate) to the Court and opposing parties the position of the
                     Plaintiffs on all matters arising during pretrial (and, if appropriate, trial)
9                    proceedings;
10                e. Serve as the primary contact for all communications between Plaintiffs and
                     Defendant, and act as spokespersons for all Plaintiffs vis-à-vis Defendant and
11                   the Court;
12                f. Direct and execute on behalf of Plaintiffs the filing of pleadings and other
                     documents with the Court;
13
                  g. Appear at all court hearings and conferences regarding the case as most
14                   appropriate for effective and efficient representation, and speak for Plaintiffs at
                     all such hearings and conferences;
15
                  h. Receive and initiate communication with the Court and the Clerk of the Court
16                   (including receiving orders, notices, correspondence and telephone calls) and
                     dispensing the content of such communications among Plaintiffs’ counsel;
17
                  i. Initiate and conduct discussions and negotiations with counsel for Defendant
18                   on all matters, including settlement;
19                j. Negotiate and enter into stipulations with opposing counsel as necessary for the
                     conduct of the litigation;
20
                  k. Initiate, coordinate and conduct all discovery on Plaintiffs’ behalf and ensuring
21                   its efficiency;
22                l. Select, consult with and employ experts for Plaintiffs, as necessary;
23                m. Encourage and enforce efficiency among all Plaintiffs’ counsel;
24                n. Assess Plaintiffs’ counsel for the costs of the litigation;
25                o. Prepare and distribute periodic status reports to the Court and to the parties as
                     ordered;
26
              p. Develop and recommend for Court approval practices and procedures
27               pertaining to attorneys’ fees and expenses as further detailed below and, on an
                 ongoing basis, monitor and administer such procedures. At such time as may
28               be appropriate, Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel also will recommend
                                               -3-

1                    apportionment and allocation of any fees and expenses that might become due
                     to Plaintiffs’ counsel in this matter; and
2
                  q. Perform such other duties as are necessary in connection with the prosecution
3                    of this litigation or as may be further directed by the Court.
4
5    SO ORDERED:

                                                     1          Pursuant to L.R. 6-1(b), Plaintiff Julie Dolphin (“Plaintiff”) and Defendants Hims, Inc. and
                                                     2   Hims & Hers Health, Inc. (“Defendants”) (collectively, the “Parties”), by and through their counsel
                                                     3   of record, hereby stipulate and agree as follows (“Stipulation”):
                                                     4          WHEREAS, Plaintiff Dolphin filed her Complaint on April 10, 2026, Dolphin v. Hims &
                                                     5   Hers, Inc., United States District Court, Northern District of California, Case No. 3:26-cv-03077-
                                                     6   CRB (incorrectly sued as “Hims and Hers, Inc.”), which has not yet been served;
                                                     7          WHEREAS, a separate plaintiff, Hoagland-Sweeney filed his First Amended Class Action
                                                     8   Complaint (“FAC”) on April 15, 2026, Hoagland-Sweeney v. Hims, Inc. and Hims & Hers Health,
                                                     9   Inc., United States District Court, Northern District of California, Case No. 4:26-cv-03157-KAW;
                                                    10          WHEREAS, Defendants were served with Hoagland-Sweeney’s FAC on May 8, 2026;
                                                    11          WHEREAS, Defendants’ original deadline to respond to the FAC was May 29, 2026;
B AKER & H OSTE TLER LLP




                                                    12          WHEREAS, on April 21, 2026, Hoagland-Sweeney filed a Notice of Related Actions
   A TTORNEYS AT LAW
                           SAN FRANCISCO
       B AKER & H




                                                    13   identifying Dolphin v. Hims & Hers, Inc., Case No. 4:26-cv-03077-KAW as related;
                                           NGELES




                                                    14          WHEREAS, on May 11, 2026, Plaintiff Julie Dolphin filed an Administrative Motion to
                                                    15   Relate Cases requesting the court to relate her action to Hoagland-Sweeney’s action;
                                                    16          WHEREAS, on May 18, 2026, the Court granted Plaintiff Julie Dolphin’s Administrative
                                                    17   Motion to Relate Cases;
                                                    18          WHEREAS, on May 29, 2026, Hoagland-Sweeney and Defendants entered into a
                                                    19   stipulation to extend Defendants’ deadline to respond to Plaintiff’s FAC in the Hoagland-Sweeney
                                                    20   action to June 29, 2026, because both Hoagland-Sweeney and Julie Dolphin indicated their intent
                                                    21   to file a motion to consolidate the related actions;
                                                    22          WHEREAS, on June 8, 2026, Plaintiff Julie Dolphin filed a Motion to Consolidate Cases
                                                    23   and For Appointment of Interim Co-Lead Class Counsel (“Motion to Consolidate”), requesting that
                                                    24   the Dolphin and Hoagland-Sweeney cases be consolidated, that Dolphin be designated as the lead
                                                    25   case, and that the Hoagland-Sweeney case be closed.
                                                    26          WHEREAS, on June 17, 2026, Defendants filed their Non-Opposition to Plaintiff Julie
                                                    27   Dolphin’s Motion to Consolidate, indicating that Defendants do not oppose consolidation and take
                                                    28   no position on the appointment of interim co-lead class counsel.
                                                                                                           2
                                                                     STIPULATION AND [PROPOSED] ORDER VACATING EXISTING DEADLINES PENDING THE COURT’S RULING ON

                                                          Case 3:26-cv-03077-CRB              Document 22         Filed 06/30/26     Page 3 of 5



                                                     1          WHEREAS, on June 25, 2026, Hoagland-Sweeney and Defendants entered into a
                                                     2   stipulation to vacate the existing deadlines pending the Court’s ruling on consolidation and to
                                                     3   extend Defendants’ responsive pleading deadline until thirty (30) days after the filing of a
                                                     4   consolidated complaint if the Court grants the Motion to Consolidate, or, if the Court denies the
                                                     5   Motion to Consolidate, thirty (30) days after the Court’s denial;
                                                     6          WHEREAS, the Hoagland-Sweeney matter is currently pending transfer to a district judge;
                                                     7          WHEREAS, the Parties agree that it would be inefficient and would potentially waste
                                                     8   judicial resources for Defendants to file separate responsive pleadings in each lawsuit prior to an
                                                     9   order on consolidation;
                                                    10          WHEREAS, the Parties agree that, pending the Court’s ruling on the Motion to Consolidate,
                                                    11   it would be beneficial to:
B AKER & H OSTE TLER LLP




                                                    12          (1) vacate the Initial Case Management Conference presently scheduled for July 14, 2026,
   A TTORNEYS AT LAW
                           SAN FRANCISCO
       B AKER & H




                                                    13   at 1:30 pm;
                                           NGELES




                                                    14          (2) vacate all deadlines to comply with ADR Certification, Rule 26(f), or provide initial
                                                    15   disclosures as identified in the Court’s Orders Setting Initial Case Management Conference and
                                                    16   ADR Deadlines; and
                                                    17          (3) extend Defendants’ deadline to respond to the complaint until either (a) thirty (30) days
                                                    18   after a consolidated complaint has been filed if the Court grants the Motion to Consolidate; or (b)
                                                    19   if the Court denies the Motion to Consolidate, thirty (30) days after the Court’s denial.
                                                    20          The Parties respectfully request that the Court enter an order accordingly.
                                                    21          IT IS SO STIPULATED.
